actualComputation.atomCounts: Parent, accepted and each candidate have 14 first-slot plus 9 second-slot atoms: 23 total. Historical cycle106's nine-atom alphabet meant only the frozen second slot, not the whole parent.
actualComputation.parentControl: Because slot0 restored the parent, both proposals start from exactly the same H/Z/target/weights/features/edges and have byte-identical stored gradient and step. oldSlot differs. They are two mappings of one parent signal, not independent specimens or two successful updates.
actualComputation.freshServing: Initializer uses four discovery cases. Final fresh stdlib child serves parent and accepted on all seven raw cases; every accepted output SHA equals the corresponding parent output SHA. The novel packet is executed but unscored, and transfer01/11 is previously inspected history.
actualComputation.sourceBoundary: Only gamma5120B was materialized for original RMS/gamma; no QKV, affine, attention, MLP, full encoder, denoiser, VAE or image evaluation. Full lexical preparation/native targets and offline learned normalization remain paid.
actualComputation.fixedPrefix: Two fixed contextual prefix rows remain supplied compiled constants; 510 rows per history are learned writers. Neither full512 accuracy nor arbitrary-prompt closure is established.

objectiveResults.scope: Numbers are four separately normalized squared-error terms and their arithmetic mean, not RMS percentages. H/Z endpoint denominators are native endpoint energies; response denominators are native pair energies. These differ from older increment-normalized headline errors.
objectiveResults.trend: Every future improves aggregate H endpoint loss, while every other aggregate term worsens. Both half-dose candidates outperform their full-dose sibling on all four terms, yet neither beats the parent jointly. This dose trend is retained; it does not authorize an automatic smaller-dose sweep.
objectiveResults.interpretation: Native Z endpoint loss is the largest adverse contribution in every future. That localizes the score tradeoff but does not causally assign it to radius, curvature, projection or finite admission.
objectiveResults.notCapacityNull: The parent itself proves a lower feasible joint score exists in the same serving grammar. This single greedy H-metric projection does not establish the best joint H/Z program or a family/dictionary lower bound.

retainedEndpointAndResponseEvidence.publicPanelScope: All 18,432 rows cover parent and accepted only: 12,288 endpoint and 6,144 pair rows, 18,432 unique keys. All accepted scalar rows equal parent exactly. The four rejected futures have complete aggregate objectives and retained remote H/Z, but no rejected-future per-row panels in this public stream; no every-row regression claim is justified.
retainedEndpointAndResponseEvidence.strata: Parent/accepted active endpoint relative RMS remains roughly H64.8-68.2%, Z81.1-86.1%; padding about H36.3-38.9%, Z34.2-37.0%. These are native endpoint-normalized, not old native-increment-normalized values.
retainedEndpointAndResponseEvidence.row9: The repeated vessel-prefix row9 retains H response relative error0.04743229799763939 and finite Z response0.7142421197803409; native endpoint-relative Z errors0.8389086691942849 and0.9137094626644082. retainedEndpointAndResponseEvidence.countertrends: Cube active response is relatively good but concentrated, cube padding remains poor and many rows lose to zero response. Vessel padding remains identically unresponsive. Exact restore preserves these heterogeneous failures; it is mechanics success, not contextual improvement.

solverAndProjection.scope: Small solve residuals support internal algebraic mechanics only. The ideal Jacobian/isotropic paired surrogate is a proposal, and projection uses the H graph rather than that full surrogate. Changed-route constant refits need not contain the parent at dose zero. Finite atom/state admission further separates the proposed and actual state steps.
solverAndProjection.featureObservation: Slot0's new route uses position, mask, causalActiveCount, first:94607, current lexical and causal-mean coordinates; slot1 uses position/current lexical/causal means. New input-dependent routes were actually constructed, but their presence alone does not establish useful propagation.

paidCosts.limits: Registry-only norm timing excludes outer hashes; parent CPU excludes child CPU. nextCut.status: one conditional recommendation, unimplemented and unqueued; full111 review/storage first
nextCut.question: Where does a useful local proposal lose its predicted descent when converted to a finite branch writer?
nextCut.fixedEvidence: Use only the two saved proposal gradient/step matrices, fixed four candidate programs/routes/FP32 atoms, parent program, retained own features, actual parent/candidate H states, frozen weights/edges/scales and published objectives. No new fit, route, atom budget, data, dose, original finite RMS, QKV or image.
nextCut.threeRepresentations: For each existing candidate c at its original dose d: unconstrained d*Delta; writer-coordinate change u_c = saved candidate slot writer - saved parent slot writer; actual full-state change v_c = saved H_c - H_parent after both finite admissions. Reconstructing u uses only admitted FP32 atoms and owned routes; it includes route/projection and atom admission. v-u includes state admission effects, including the downstream second addition when replacing slot0.
nextCut.primaryScalars: Retain g dot (d*Delta), g dot u_c, g dot v_c, and the signed mapping terms g dot (u_c-d*Delta), g dot (v_c-u_c), plus explicit floating regrouping residual. Retain norms/angles and history/active-padding contributions, rather than only one pooled sign. Preserve actual objective differences alongside these proxies.
nextCut.slopeMeaning: The stored g uses actual finite Z residuals pulled back through the declared ideal Jacobian. For the four-term mean, g dot v / 2 is an anchored ideal local-model slope. It is not a derivative of the piecewise BF16 objective, and negative slope is not a guarantee of finite improvement.
nextCut.zeroDoseCaution: 2*v_half-v_full is an admitted two-point secant intercept only. FP32 atom and BF16 state admission prevent calling it the exact new-route zero-dose baseline. A true zero-dose solve/admission would be additional declared scientific work; it is not needed for this cut.
nextCut.decisionUse: If negative unconstrained slope becomes nonnegative after route/atom projection or state admission, repair the parent-preserving joint-metric mapping before another teacher/data or budget expansion. If admitted slope remains negative while finite loss rises, curvature, ideal/finite mismatch and admission remain competing explanations; do not declare a sign bug or automatically shrink doses. A null mapping result may redirect the next construction after full111.
nextCut.paidDependencies: Any future vector reductions or route reconstruction must run in the authorized scientific lane near retained arrays, with exact source/payload authentication and explicit arithmetic cost. Optional decomposition into separate H/Z slope terms would require separately charged ideal pullback arithmetic; it is not silently free or part of the current result.
nextCut.goalRelevance: This checks whether the compiler can turn target-informed offline feedback into an input-owned branch/copy/add state program, while preserving the full prompt/state/image objective. It does not itself supply downstream contextual closure, denoising or pixel production.

overallConclusion: The declared controller correctly restored its feasible parent while retaining four complete tradeoffs. The unchanged selected writer remains an approximate content-dependent H1 constructor with severe response gaps. Neither the writer family nor the strict zero-neural arbitrary-prompt image goal is closed by this assay.
